title: Widevine device security levels and policy
content: Widevine device robustness levels are part of content-protection policy. L1 uses a hardware-backed trusted path for protected processing, while L3 relies on software-level protection. A service may require L1 for premium HD or UHD tiers. Treat the exact quality restriction as service policy, not a universal Widevine rule.

title: HDCP output protection is part of playback policy
content: Encrypted Media Extensions can expose HDCP policy checks through the CDM. If the active display path does not meet a required HDCP version, a player may restrict quality, report an output-restricted key status, or fail protected video output. Check the entire path, including display, cable, receiver, splitter, and adapter.

title: DASH CENC signaling, ContentProtection, KID, and PSSH
content: For Common Encryption content, DRM initialization data and key identifiers must be consistent with the encrypted tracks and license service. In DASH this is commonly signaled with ContentProtection descriptors, system identifiers, default_KID values, and PSSH data. A system-ID, KID, or PSSH mismatch can cause license or no-usable-key errors.

title: FairPlay Streaming and HLS key signaling
content: FairPlay Streaming protects HLS playback on Apple platforms. Diagnosis should correlate HLS key signaling, the content identifier, application certificate, SPC request, CKC response, and device/player error. Redact certificates, tokens, and full license payloads before adding them to a troubleshooting corpus.

title: PlayReady client and license-service correlation
content: PlayReady diagnosis should correlate the manifest protection header, license challenge, HTTP exchange, rights/policy response, client robustness, and output protection. A successful HTTP response alone does not prove that the returned license is usable for the selected key or policy.

title: Interpreting license HTTP failures
content: HTTP 401 or 403 during license acquisition often points to authentication, entitlement, token expiry, signature, device binding, or required headers. HTTP 5xx usually shifts investigation toward the license service or its dependencies. Always correlate a redacted request ID with server logs; never store reusable authorization tokens in the knowledge base.

title: Representation codec versus device decoder capability
content: A manifest can advertise representations the device cannot decode reliably. Compare the actually selected representation with the device hardware-decoder capability, profile, level, bit depth, HDR format, and secure-decoder requirement. Force a known-compatible AVC rendition to separate DRM failure from decoder failure.

title: Distinguishing CDN failure from DRM failure
content: If the manifest and license succeed but segments or chunks return 403, 404, 5xx, or timeouts, inspect signed-URL expiry, cache keys, regional routing, origin availability, range requests, and clock skew. Compare failing media URLs and request IDs across a working and failing session.

title: Use ABR and rendition forcing as a diagnostic control
content: Force a single known-good rendition to reduce variables. If 1080p AVC works but 4K HEVC fails, investigate UHD policy, secure decoder, codec/profile, HDR, and HDCP before blaming the whole asset or CDN. Record the chosen representation rather than only the manifest's available representations.

title: Black screen is a symptom, not a root cause
content: A black screen can result from output protection, unusable keys, secure-surface configuration, decoder failure, HDR/display negotiation, or an application rendering bug. Determine whether audio plays, whether frames decode, the key status, the selected representation, and whether the video surface is secure before assigning a cause.

title: Widevine: robustness negotiation
content: Compare requested EME robustness with the CDM response and service policy. A rejected robustness string can prevent session creation before any license request. Capture only redacted evidence and document the discriminating test and observed result.

title: Widevine: offline licenses
content: For offline playback, verify persistent-license support, stored key-set identifiers, expiry, renewal, and device clock. Reproduce with a freshly downloaded title. Capture only redacted evidence and document the discriminating test and observed result.

title: Widevine: secure surfaces
content: On Android, correlate MediaCrypto, secure decoder requirements, and the rendering surface. A license can be usable while frames cannot reach a protected output surface. Capture only redacted evidence and document the discriminating test and observed result.

title: Widevine: provisioning
content: Separate provisioning failures from content-license failures. Capture the CDM provisioning state and retry on a known-good network without storing provisioning payloads. Capture only redacted evidence and document the discriminating test and observed result.

title: FairPlay: SPC and CKC correlation
content: Trace content identifier, application certificate, SPC generation, CKC HTTP response, and AVContentKeySession processing as one request chain. Capture only redacted evidence and document the discriminating test and observed result.

title: FairPlay: certificate validation
content: Confirm the correct FairPlay application certificate is selected for the environment and that certificate bytes are delivered without text encoding changes. Capture only redacted evidence and document the discriminating test and observed result.

title: FairPlay: offline keys
content: Validate persistable content-key requests, storage lifecycle, rental expiry, and renewal behavior separately from online streaming playback. Capture only redacted evidence and document the discriminating test and observed result.

title: FairPlay: AirPlay output
content: When playback differs during AirPlay or external display use, compare route changes, output-protection state, selected rendition, and CoreMedia errors. Capture only redacted evidence and document the discriminating test and observed result.

title: PlayReady: security levels
content: Compare the client security level and hardware DRM capability with the license policy and selected UHD representation. Capture only redacted evidence and document the discriminating test and observed result.

title: PlayReady: protection headers
content: Decode the PlayReady Object or protection header and compare KIDs, license URL, custom data, and packaging output. Capture only redacted evidence and document the discriminating test and observed result.

title: PlayReady: individualization
content: Distinguish client individualization or provisioning errors from license authorization failures by testing the same account on a known-good client. Capture only redacted evidence and document the discriminating test and observed result.

title: PlayReady: output restrictions
content: Inspect license output-protection levels and the active display chain; an HTTP 200 license response can still carry rights that restrict playback. Capture only redacted evidence and document the discriminating test and observed result.

title: HLS: playlist continuity
content: Check media sequence, discontinuity sequence, target duration, segment timeline, and live-window updates when playback stalls or jumps. Capture only redacted evidence and document the discriminating test and observed result.

title: HLS: FairPlay key tags
content: Validate EXT-X-KEY or EXT-X-SESSION-KEY method, KEYFORMAT, URI, key rotation boundaries, and content identifier mapping. Capture only redacted evidence and document the discriminating test and observed result.

title: HLS: low latency
content: For LL-HLS, correlate partial segments, preload hints, blocking reloads, rendition reports, cache behavior, and player hold-back settings. Capture only redacted evidence and document the discriminating test and observed result.

title: HLS: variant compatibility
content: Verify CODECS and RESOLUTION declarations describe the actual media and that the player filters unsupported variants before ABR selection. Capture only redacted evidence and document the discriminating test and observed result.

title: MPEG-DASH: timeline validation
content: Inspect SegmentTemplate, SegmentTimeline, timescale, presentationTimeOffset, period boundaries, and availability windows for gaps or overlaps. Capture only redacted evidence and document the discriminating test and observed result.

title: MPEG-DASH: content protection
content: Compare ContentProtection system IDs, default_KID, PSSH boxes, encrypted-track KIDs, and the license key database. Capture only redacted evidence and document the discriminating test and observed result.

title: MPEG-DASH: dynamic MPD
content: For live DASH, verify availabilityStartTime, publishTime, minimumUpdatePeriod, timeShiftBufferDepth, and client clock synchronization. Capture only redacted evidence and document the discriminating test and observed result.

title: MPEG-DASH: representation selection
content: Record the selected AdaptationSet and Representation, codec string, profile, level, bandwidth, HDR metadata, and secure-decoder requirement. Capture only redacted evidence and document the discriminating test and observed result.

title: HDCP: display chain isolation
content: Test direct-to-display before adding receivers, splitters, docks, adapters, or capture hardware. Record the negotiated HDCP version at each topology. Capture only redacted evidence and document the discriminating test and observed result.

title: HDCP: output-restricted keys
content: Treat output-restricted key status as direct evidence that license output policy and the current display path are incompatible. Capture only redacted evidence and document the discriminating test and observed result.

title: HDCP: hot-plug changes
content: Capture HDMI hot-plug and route-change events because HDCP renegotiation can invalidate a previously working protected playback session. Capture only redacted evidence and document the discriminating test and observed result.

title: HDCP: resolution fallback
content: Test whether an allowed HD or SD tier plays on the same path. Successful fallback separates output policy from general license or CDN failure. Capture only redacted evidence and document the discriminating test and observed result.

title: CENC/PSSH: system ID mapping
content: Identify every PSSH system ID and ensure the intended DRM client receives compatible initialization data. Capture only redacted evidence and document the discriminating test and observed result.

title: CENC/PSSH: key rotation
content: At rotation boundaries, compare new KIDs, PSSH updates, license keys, segment encryption metadata, and player session renewal behavior. Capture only redacted evidence and document the discriminating test and observed result.

title: CENC/PSSH: scheme compatibility
content: Confirm cenc or cbcs scheme support across packager, manifest, DRM, player, and device; do not infer scheme support from codec support. Capture only redacted evidence and document the discriminating test and observed result.

title: CENC/PSSH: track inspection
content: Inspect tenc, schm, saiz, saio, senc, and sample-group signaling when manifest metadata appears correct but decryption still fails. Capture only redacted evidence and document the discriminating test and observed result.

title: License acquisition: authorization headers
content: Compare redacted working and failing requests for bearer-token freshness, cookies, custom data, origin, device binding, and required headers. Capture only redacted evidence and document the discriminating test and observed result.

title: License acquisition: HTTP status triage
content: Use 401 and 403 for authorization investigation, 429 for rate limiting, and 5xx for service dependency investigation, then correlate request IDs. Capture only redacted evidence and document the discriminating test and observed result.

title: License acquisition: usable rights
content: After HTTP success, inspect CDM processing, key status, expiry, output restrictions, and KID coverage; transport success is not license usability. Capture only redacted evidence and document the discriminating test and observed result.

title: License acquisition: clock and expiry
content: Validate device clock, token not-before and expiry, license duration, playback duration, and renewal timing for intermittent authorization failures. Capture only redacted evidence and document the discriminating test and observed result.

title: CDN: signed URL preservation
content: Trace redirects and manifest-relative URL resolution to ensure signed query parameters and authorization headers reach every media request. Capture only redacted evidence and document the discriminating test and observed result.

title: CDN: range requests
content: Compare Range request and Content-Range response behavior at edge and origin when fragmented MP4 initialization or seeking fails. Capture only redacted evidence and document the discriminating test and observed result.

title: CDN: regional isolation
content: Run identical probes from working and failing regions, preserving DNS, edge POP, cache status, request ID, status, and origin timing. Capture only redacted evidence and document the discriminating test and observed result.

title: CDN: cache correctness
content: Include DRM and rendition-varying request attributes in cache analysis to prevent stale manifests, wrong keys, or cross-policy response reuse. Capture only redacted evidence and document the discriminating test and observed result.

title: Player errors: error normalization
content: Map native player, OS, CDM, manifest, decoder, and network errors into a common taxonomy while retaining the original code and timestamp. Capture only redacted evidence and document the discriminating test and observed result.

title: Player errors: fatal versus retryable
content: Record severity, retry count, backoff, recovery action, and final state so transient network events are not mistaken for fatal DRM failures. Capture only redacted evidence and document the discriminating test and observed result.

title: Player errors: session correlation
content: Join manifest, license, segment, decoder, and render events with one session identifier and a monotonic timeline. Capture only redacted evidence and document the discriminating test and observed result.

title: Player errors: known-good control
content: Repeat the same asset and account on a known-good device and repeat a known-good asset on the failing device to isolate asset versus client scope. Capture only redacted evidence and document the discriminating test and observed result.
